summary: Nora's position in a room keeps the threads she is holding and knows how old it is, and it is no longer thrown away by a second model's judgement.
details: The post-turn fold is one model call: the grounding verdict that ran beside it, and the re-derivations it triggered, are removed. A re-derivation rewrote the position without showing the model the previous one, so each one dropped the threads she was holding.
The fold is shown tool results up to 4000 characters instead of 600, and is told they survive only through what it writes.

The previous position is shown with how long ago it was written, every message the fold reads carries its date, and the fold is told to write dates instead of words like today or tomorrow, so a stale clause can be recognised and dropped.
The turn's steps are shown as they are: private reasoning appears, marked, only when the model produced any.
What the fold stores is screened more strictly before it is kept: emails, long platform ids and labelled coordinates are refused as well as phone numbers and coordinate pairs.
limitations: The [standing] rebuild_after_folds key is removed; a config that still sets it refuses to start.
The turn_verdict table and standing.consumed_verdict_tag column are left in place with no writer.
Keeping what she found but did not send is not achieved yet: measured on real turns, the fold still leaves those findings out (issue #445).
